**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `afa8659318d1663dd9af27e5f24be5d91ba65b00`.

Small delta from `9cdcf3d8fac96966067901d6b8966d1cf76b844b`, carrying forward [round 3](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/pull/167#issuecomment-6714315003), governance `cc7c4c6`, and its referenced full cost review.

**New cost:** the wake mark replaces the existing settlement UPDATE with a guarded UPDATE in the same schema-checked owned write transaction. Its correlated `NOT EXISTS` asks only whether this seat has a higher-sequence pending compaction. Equality on `seat`, a range on `seq`, and `settled IS NULL` match the existing `(seat, seq)` partial index; existence needs no returned payload or materialized row list. The outer `(seat, msg_id)` lookup remains UNIQUE. This adds index-compatible existence work inside the write critical section, not another application SELECT, transaction, roster read or history sweep. No local query-plan or production-duration measurement is claimed.

The guard is reached only by `Step::Wake`, after the existing delivery/activity/age/idle/queue/holdings checks. **Empty steady-state work is unchanged:** one pending-index query plus its schema check per existing nominal 60-second watchdog round. No new loop, timer, poll or executable site; the owned Tokio write task replaces the prior one rather than adding a task per mark.

**Once per wake-mark attempt, not necessarily once per compaction:** a newer pending row vetoes the mark, leaves the older row pending and sends nothing. A later eligible round can retry; every such attempt still acquires and commits the existing write transaction and pays the predicate. Errors are logged and also leave the row pending. No retry cap or pending-row bound was added. Successful marks still remove the row from the pending index before the existing one-send path; the at-most-one-attempt delivery qualification stands.

**CI:** [42425691985](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42425691985) succeeds at this exact SHA, with Rust lint/test and Node 22/24 checks. Downloaded JUnit records **2,183 executed cases, zero failures/errors**: the new store guard regression, all **ten daemon compaction cases**, the core message case and **six launch guards** pass. The new store case reads A, records newer B, verifies A's mark is refused and remains pending, settles B undelivered, then verifies A can mark exactly once despite another seat's pending row. This is store-level behavior proof, not a live concurrent wake/latency benchmark. Delivers `42425694625` succeeds; the cancelled duplicate is not proof.

The worktree is clean and its HEAD matches GitHub's CLEAN/MERGEABLE head.
